name: JonDash official addons
description: Official add-on modules and helpers for JonDash. In JonDash, add this repo as a module source (Admin -> Modules -> Manage sources) to browse and install. Modules update independently of the JonDash base app. Channels: the main branch = stable; this manifest (beta branch) = beta. See VERSIONING.md.

modules.name: Health monitoring
modules.description: Watches your services with HTTP, TCP, ping, DNS and certificate checks, records uptime and response times, and alerts by email or webhook when something goes down.
modules.notes: Housekeeping only — monitoring behaves exactly as before. Corrects the JonDash version this module says it needs, which named the release where it should have named the pre-release, and repairs a shipped test that no longer compiled against JonDash 1.5.2.

modules.name: Module template (for developers)
modules.description: FOR DEVELOPERS — a working example to copy when building your own module. Installs to modules/template; open MODULE.md in that folder for a full guide, and AI-PROMPT.md to have an AI build one for you. Safe to install, and safe to uninstall when you're done.
modules.notes: The template depends on nothing: no helpers and no background work, so copying it gives you a module that installs on its own. Adds a done toggle — showing a follow-up migration and a permission the code actually uses — and a fuller guide, including a paste-in AI prompt for building a module.

modules.name: Backup Manager
modules.description: Keeps folders copied to another location — a network share or an external drive — on a schedule, and tells you what it did. Can keep dated copies and tidy old ones away automatically.
modules.notes: Follows the Files and folders helper, which can now be allowed every folder on the machine rather than an approved list. Backups, schedules and approved folders all carry over unchanged.

modules.name: Host vitals
modules.description: Shows how this server is doing — CPU, memory, how full each disk is, uptime and temperatures — as a dashboard tile and a page.
modules.notes: Follows the System metrics helper onto JonDash's new Permissions screen. Nothing about the readings has changed.

modules.name: Service control
modules.description: Start, stop and restart the services you approve — a Windows service, a systemd unit — from your dashboard, without opening a terminal.
modules.notes: Follows the Host services helper onto JonDash's new Permissions screen. The page now says plainly which services it can act on and which it can only look at, which was misleading when you allow it to see every service.

modules.name: Docker manager
modules.description: See the containers on this server and start, stop, pause and restart them. Shows you how to install Docker if it isn't set up yet, and can install it for you.
modules.notes: Follows the Docker helper onto JonDash's new Permissions screen. Nothing about managing containers has changed.

helpers.name: Scheduler
helpers.description: Runs modules' declared background work on time, starting when the server starts rather than when someone opens a page.
helpers.notes: Corrects the JonDash version this helper says it needs, which named the release where it should have named the pre-release. The helper itself is unchanged.

helpers.name: Files and folders
helpers.description: Lets a module copy and archive folders to another location — a network share, an external drive — within the folders you allow. JonDash's own secrets are never copied.

provides.label: Look at files and folders in the locations you allow
Create and change files in the locations you allow
Delete files in the locations you allow

helpers.notes: Adds an 'allow everything' option — separately for reading, changing and deleting — so a module can be given the run of the machine without approving folders one at a time. JonDash's own data stays protected unless you switch that off, and it says what that exposes.

helpers.name: System metrics
helpers.description: Reads this server's CPU, memory, disk usage, uptime and (where available) temperatures, so a module can show them. Read-only — it changes nothing on the host.

provides.label: See this server's CPU, memory, disk usage, uptime and temperature

helpers.notes: Shows up properly on JonDash's new Permissions screen, with a plain name and a risk level. Nothing about how it works has changed.

helpers.name: Host services
helpers.description: Lets a module see and control the services you list — a Windows service, a systemd unit — so a dashboard can restart something without you opening a terminal. Only the services you add, and only start, stop and restart.

provides.label: See whether the services you list are running
Start, stop and restart the services you list

helpers.notes: Approved services now appear on JonDash's new Permissions screen, where you can search for a service instead of typing its name, and choose per service whether a module may act on it without asking you. You can also allow modules to see every service, which never lets them start or stop anything.

helpers.name: Docker
helpers.description: Lets a module see the containers on this server and start, stop, pause and restart them. It cannot run commands inside a container, create or delete one, or touch images and volumes.

provides.label: See the containers on this server — their names, images, state and resource use
Read container logs, which often contain passwords, keys and personal data
Start, stop, pause and restart containers on this server

helpers.notes: Shows up properly on JonDash's new Permissions screen, with plain names and a risk level for each thing it can do. Reading container logs is now marked as the serious one it is, since logs often contain passwords and keys. Nothing about how it works has changed.

helpers.name: Install software
helpers.description: Installs and removes software on this server using Windows' own package manager, with your permission each time. JonDash only ever offers to remove software it installed itself.

provides.label: See whether a piece of software is installed on this server
Install and remove software on this server — you approve each one, and see its name before it runs

helpers.notes: Shows up properly on JonDash's new Permissions screen, with plain names and a risk level for each thing it can do. Nothing about how it works has changed — every install is still approved by you, one at a time, with the package name on screen.
